column1: Report title: Probation and Parole in the United States, 2017-2018  NCJ 252072
Data Source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Annual Probation Survey, 2018; and U.S. Census Bureau, National Intercensal Estimates, 2019
Authors: Danielle Kaeble, BJS Statistician, and Mariel Alper, Ph.D., former BJS Statistician

column15: Number on probation per 100,000 U.S. adult residents, December 31, 2018/b

column1: Note: Data quality may vary across jurisdictions for counts of entries and exits. Therefore, the population on December 31, 2018 does not equal the population on January 1, 2018, plus entries, minus exits. Counts may not be actual as reporting agencies may provide estimates on some or all detailed data. Rates are based on the probation population counts as of December 31 of the reporting year and were calculated using U.S. Census Bureau estimates of the U.S. resident population of persons age 18 or older for January 1 of the following year.
a/Reported data will equal estimated data in cases where no imputation was required.
b/Rates were calculated using the estimated U.S. adult resident population in each jurisdiction on January 1, 2019.
c/See Probation: Explanatory notes for 2018 for more details.
d/The only exits reported were deaths.
Source: Bureau of Justice Statistics, Annual Probation Survey, 2018; and U.S. Census Bureau, National Intercensal Estimates, 2019.
